sources.method: Reused current batch-1 record and read retained full README text; not refetched.
sources.scope: Default-branch documentation, not demonstrated release behavior
excerpts: Leaves is a disk usage analyzer inspired by WinDirStat and QDirStat. It shows files and directories in a hierarchy of nested rectangles.
this will work over remote shell connections when graphical desktop environments are not available or impractical.
A Rust toolchain is required to build this project.
By default, hidden directories will be ignored. Additionally, anything matching patterns in .gitignore or .ignore files in the hierarchy will not be counted.
You can disable all ignore rules with -A.
leaves will not follow symbolic links since they don't incur additional disk usage inside the directory. No attempt is made to detect hard links, so they will be double counted.
However, due to the limited resolution of working at a character level, this is a fairly coarse approximation compared to a graphical tool.

workflow.primaryIntent: Understand Leaves ignore/link semantics and whether the scan is of a remote Linux host or the local Mac before choosing a maintenance tool.
workflow.leadDirection: A terminal treemap is a map of its selected host and scan rules, not permission to delete large files or proof of local Mac recoverable space.

leavesAdvantages.judgment: Better documented fit for terminal/remote-shell treemap inspection, including configurable ignore rules.

leavesTradeoffs.judgment: Character-cell sizing is approximate; hard links can inflate counts. Verified release binaries are Linux-only in the inspected records; native Mac runtime unverified.

breathingRoomAdvantages.judgment: Broader documented local Mac-maintenance scope: storage views and app/process grouping with reviewable cleanup architecture, if a preview and its requirements suit the reader.

breathingRoomTradeoffs.judgment: Not a verified replacement for remote Linux treemaps; preview/notarization/Python caveats matter. Hosted AI needs account/network and optional paid care is distinct from free local features.
